GTK Free E-Book of the Week (12.18.16 - 12.25.16): The Turner Diaries by Andrew Macdonald

So I figured since I just finished this book the first time this morning, I'd give you a personal review.

First off, I immensely enjoyed this book. It is not poorly written at all. Andrew Macdonald's (the pseudonym of the author) real name is William Pierce and he's a physicist.

So with that aside, the book reminds me a lot of 1984-meets-Red Dawn. The protagonist, Earl Turner, was arrested during a gun raid after all firearms are banned in the year 1991. After his brief arrest, he joins an anti-government organization and gives up his life as an electrical engineer. His organization regularly conducts terror-style attacks on the new communist "egalitarian" government. The book is written as his diary during the years the organization operates. Earl's specialty is communication and he serves as a sort of communications engineer/jack of all trades in the organization. He builds bombs, detonators, enables radio communications between branches of the group, and even handles some of the dirtier work.

With fake IDs and disguises, the group is able to inflict a fair amount of damage to the government and constantly works to undermine the new Communist US government. In many ways, it's like a handbook for what to do in such an event - even giving thinly veiled instruction to the reader as to such an overthrow of the government.

The only real drawback is timeline created by the author. The events take place in 1991 and the book was written in the 1970s, so you must read between the lines and ignore some of the time-sensitive materials in the book, but I'm not sure if Pierce knew that his book would endure the time it has. Other than that, I found the book to be probably the definitive piece of fiction for those who dream about the DotR. If you enjoy this subverse, you'd very likely enjoy this book very much. I broke it up during several days of listening to the audiobook and found myself wishing it didn't end.

I give the book a solid B+.
